headline: Failed Senate resolution would have canceled a Treasury rule letting state and local governments count COVID relief paperwork costs as committed by the 2024 deadline.
what_it_does: This resolution would have canceled a Treasury Department rule from November 2023 about COVID-19 relief money given to state and local governments under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021. Governments must commit (obligate) this money by December 31, 2024, and spend it by December 31, 2026. The rule lets them count money set aside for required program tasks, such as reporting, audits, and environmental reviews, as committed by the 2024 deadline. Canceling the rule would have removed that option.

who_it_affects.group: State, local, tribal, and territorial governments that received COVID-19 recovery funds
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost the ability to count estimated costs for reporting, audits, and environmental compliance as committed by the December 31, 2024 deadline.
Its rule defining what counts as committed funds for this program would have been canceled.
